issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Milkable.messageOnMilk() should return a String (the text "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). However, the solution repository defines the Milkable interface to return a boolean and the Seal and Goat classes implement messageOnMilk() returning boolean (printing the message and returning true). This return-type mismatch contradicts the specification and will confuse students about the expected signature and what to implement; it also prevents straightforward use of the method as a String-producing method in tests or the song logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface and implementations with the problem statement: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String, and update Goat and Seal to return the formatted String (e.g. "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning boolean. Alternatively, if boolean was intended, update the problem statement/UML to specify a boolean return and adjust the descriptive text accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Milkable.messageOnMilk() to produce a String message (the problem explicitly states messageOnMilk() should return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" and the template Main() calls System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk())). However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with a boolean return type and implementations (Seal, Goat) print the message internally and return true. This mismatch in the method contract for the same conceptual operation (milking an animal) creates confusion: students are instructed to implement/consume a String-returning method but the reference solution uses a boolean-returning method and side-effect printing instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable.messageOnMilk() contract consistent with the problem statement and template by changing its return type to String. Update the Milkable interface to 'String messageOnMilk();' and modify Seal and Goat to return the formatted string (e.g., "Seal Clarabelle is milked") instead of printing it internally. Adjust any calls (e.g., System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk())) to print the returned String. Alternatively, if a boolean return was intended, update the problem statement and template examples to expect a boolean and not rely on a returned String.
